concepts.name: The Next.js app router: pages, layouts, Server and Client Components

questions.prompt: In a Next.js app router project, which file renders the page at `/dashboard/settings`?

choices.text: `app/dashboard/settings/page.tsx`
`pages/dashboard/settings.tsx`
`app/dashboard/settings/route.tsx`
`app/dashboard/settings/layout.tsx`

questions.explanation: The app router uses the file system: folders are route segments and a `page` file makes the route public. A `layout` wraps pages and keeps its state on navigation, but isn't the page itself. `route` files are route handlers, and `pages/` is the older Pages Router.

sources.title: Getting Started: Layouts and Pages
sources.claim: In the app router, folders define route segments and a page file inside them makes the route publicly accessible; layouts are shared UI that preserve state on navigation.

questions.prompt: Your `app/page.tsx` calls `useChat()` and `useState()`, and Next.js errors when rendering it. What's the fix?

choices.text: Rename the file to `page.client.tsx` so that Next.js renders it in the browser
Move the component into `components/`, which Next.js renders on the client
Add `'use client'` at the top, since pages are Server Components by default
Make the component `async` so its hooks run after the server render

questions.explanation: In the app router, layouts and pages are Server Components by default. State, event handlers, effects, browser APIs and custom hooks like `useChat` need a Client Component, which you mark with `'use client'`. Keep the directive on the smallest component that needs it.

sources.title: Getting Started: Server and Client Components
sources.claim: Layouts and pages are Server Components by default; state, event handlers, effects, browser APIs and custom hooks need a Client Component marked with 'use client', added to specific interactive components.

questions.prompt: Where do you put a handler for `POST /api/chat` in a Next.js app router project?

choices.text: `app/api/chat/page.tsx`, exporting a `POST` function
`app/api/chat/route.ts`, exporting a `POST` function
`app/api/chat.ts`, with a default export handling the request
`app/api/chat/layout.ts`, exporting a `POST` function

questions.explanation: Route handlers live in a `route.ts` file and export one function per HTTP method (`GET`, `POST` and so on) that takes a Web `Request` and returns a `Response`. They're the app router's equivalent of API routes. A default export in a plain file is not a route handler.

sources.title: Getting Started: Route Handlers
sources.claim: Route Handlers are defined in a route.js|ts file in app, export functions named after HTTP methods such as POST, use the Web Request and Response APIs, and replace API Routes.

questions.prompt: What happens if a folder contains both `page.tsx` and `route.ts`?

choices.text: The page handles `GET` and the route handler handles the other methods
The route handler wins, and the page is ignored
Both run and their output is combined
It's a conflict: a `route` file can't be at the same route segment as a `page` file

questions.explanation: Each `route` or `page` file takes over all HTTP verbs for its route, so the two can't share a segment. Put API handlers under their own path, such as `app/api/chat/route.ts`, next to `app/page.tsx`.

sources.title: Getting Started: Route Handlers
sources.claim: There cannot be a route file at the same route segment as a page file; each route or page takes over all HTTP verbs for that route, and the combination is a conflict.

questions.prompt: What is a Next.js route handler, and would your chat UI need one if the agent itself runs in FastAPI?

model_answer.summary: A route handler is a `route.ts` file that answers HTTP requests with the Web `Request`/`Response` APIs. With a FastAPI backend you either call FastAPI directly or add a thin route handler (or a rewrite) that forwards to it.
key_points: A `route.ts` file in `app/` exports one function per HTTP method and uses the Web `Request` and `Response` APIs
It's the lowest-level routing primitive: it doesn't take part in layouts, and can't share a segment with a `page`
Route handlers aren't cached by default; only `GET` can opt in, and `POST` is never cached
With FastAPI you can call it directly (setting up CORS if the origin differs), or proxy through a route handler or `rewrites`, which can also keep secrets on the server

questions.explanation: A thin route handler in front of FastAPI keeps the browser talking to one origin and lets the Next.js server add credentials the browser should never see.

sources.title: Getting Started: Route Handlers
sources.claim: Route handlers are the lowest-level routing primitive, don't participate in layouts, can't share a segment with a page, aren't cached by default, and only GET can opt in to caching.

sources.title: next.config.js: rewrites
sources.claim: Rewrites map a request path to another destination, act as a URL proxy, and can target an external URL.

questions.prompt: With `useChat()` from `@ai-sdk/react` and no options, where are messages sent?

choices.text: An HTTP POST to `/api/chat`, via `DefaultChatTransport`
A WebSocket opened to `/api/chat` when the component mounts
Straight from the browser to the model provider's API
An HTTP GET to `/chat`, with the messages in the query string

questions.explanation: The default transport is `DefaultChatTransport` with `api: '/api/chat'`, which POSTs the messages. Pass your own `DefaultChatTransport` to change the URL, headers, body or credentials, or a custom transport for other protocols.

sources.title: AI SDK UI: Chatbot
sources.claim: useChat uses DefaultChatTransport with the /api/chat endpoint by default, and the endpoint, headers, body and credentials can be customised.

questions.prompt: Why does the AI SDK recommend rendering `message.parts` rather than a single content string?

choices.text: `parts` lets React re-render only the words that changed, so it's faster
`parts` holds typed pieces like text and tool calls, so each renders differently
A content string is only filled in after the whole stream has ended and been parsed
`parts` is required for messages to be serialised from Server Components

questions.explanation: UI messages carry a `parts` array, and each part has a `type`: `text`, tool parts, reasoning and so on. Rendering by part type is how a chat UI shows "calling search..." or a tool's result inline, not only the text.

sources.title: AI SDK UI: Chatbot
sources.claim: UI messages have a parts property holding typed parts such as text, tool invocations and tool results, and rendering by parts is recommended.

questions.prompt: `useChat` returns `status`. Which value means the response is actively arriving, which is when you show a Stop button?

choices.text: `submitted`
`ready`
`error`
`streaming`

questions.explanation: `submitted` means the message was sent and you're waiting for the stream to start; `streaming` means chunks are arriving; `ready` means the response is complete and a new message can be sent; `error` means the request failed. `stop()` aborts the current response.

sources.title: AI SDK UI: Chatbot
sources.claim: status is submitted while awaiting the stream start, streaming while chunks arrive, ready when complete, error when the request failed; stop() aborts the response.

questions.prompt: Explain what happens between calling `sendMessage` from `useChat` and the answer appearing word by word on screen.

model_answer.summary: `useChat` adds the user message, POSTs the conversation through its transport, and updates the assistant message's parts as each stream chunk arrives. `status` tracks each stage.
key_points: `sendMessage` adds the user's message to `messages` and sends the conversation to the endpoint through the transport (by default a POST to `/api/chat`)
`status` is `submitted` until the response stream starts, then `streaming`
Each chunk of the stream updates the assistant message's `parts`, and React re-renders, so text appears as it arrives
`status` becomes `ready` when the response is complete, or `error` if it failed; `stop()` aborts it

questions.explanation: Knowing these stages is what lets you build a good streaming UI: a spinner while `submitted`, a Stop button while `streaming`, and the input enabled when `ready`.

sources.title: AI SDK UI: Chatbot
sources.claim: sendMessage sends the message to the endpoint through the transport and streams the response back, with status moving from submitted to streaming to ready (or error) and stop() aborting.

questions.prompt: Your FastAPI endpoint streams SSE, but `useChat` (default transport) shows nothing. What does a custom backend need to send?

choices.text: Plain text chunks with `Content-Type: text/plain` and no SSE framing at all
One `application/json` body holding the full message once generation ends
SSE `event:` lines naming each token, sent with the `Content-Type: text/event-stream` header
SSE `data:` lines of JSON parts, the `x-vercel-ai-ui-message-stream: v1` header, a final `[DONE]`

questions.explanation: The default data stream protocol is SSE carrying typed JSON parts, such as `start`, `text-start`, `text-delta`, `text-end`, tool parts and `finish`. A custom backend must set `x-vercel-ai-ui-message-stream: v1`, and the stream ends with a literal `[DONE]`.

sources.title: AI SDK UI: Stream Protocols
sources.claim: The UI message (data) stream protocol is SSE carrying JSON parts such as start, text-start/delta/end, tool parts and finish; custom backends must send the x-vercel-ai-ui-message-stream: v1 header, and the stream ends with [DONE].

questions.prompt: Your FastAPI endpoint only streams plain text chunks. How do you connect `useChat` to it, and what do you give up?

choices.text: Use `TextStreamChatTransport`; you get text only, with no tool-call or data parts
Use the default transport; it detects plain text on its own
Use `TextStreamChatTransport`; you keep tool parts, but lose reconnection
It can't be done: `useChat` needs a Node.js backend

questions.explanation: The text stream protocol appends plain-text chunks into one reply, and `useChat` uses it through `TextStreamChatTransport`. It only carries text, so to stream tool calls or custom data parts you must implement the UI message (data) stream protocol instead.

sources.title: AI SDK UI: Stream Protocols
sources.claim: The text stream protocol streams plain text chunks, is used with TextStreamChatTransport, and only supports basic text, so tool calls need the data stream protocol.

questions.prompt: Describe how you connect a Next.js `useChat` UI to your FastAPI SSE endpoint. What does each side have to do?

model_answer.summary: Point `useChat`'s transport at the FastAPI endpoint (directly or through a proxy), and have FastAPI read the posted messages and stream the AI SDK's UI message protocol back.
key_points: Mark the chat component `'use client'` and configure `useChat` with a `DefaultChatTransport` whose `api` is the FastAPI URL, or a Next.js route handler or rewrite that proxies to it
FastAPI reads the POSTed JSON body, including the `messages` array whose messages carry `parts`
FastAPI streams `text/event-stream` with `data:` lines of JSON parts (text deltas, tool parts, finish) and the header `x-vercel-ai-ui-message-stream: v1`, ending with `data: [DONE]`
If the backend only streams plain text, use `TextStreamChatTransport` and accept text-only messages
If the browser calls FastAPI on another origin, FastAPI must allow it with CORS

questions.explanation: The protocol page exists for exactly this case: a backend in another language, such as Python, serving an AI SDK UI. The AI SDK repository has a Next.js plus FastAPI example.

sources.title: AI SDK UI: Stream Protocols
sources.claim: A custom (for example FastAPI) backend must stream SSE JSON parts with the x-vercel-ai-ui-message-stream: v1 header and end with [DONE], or use the text protocol with TextStreamChatTransport for text only.

sources.title: AI SDK UI: Chatbot
sources.claim: useChat's DefaultChatTransport api option sets the endpoint the conversation is sent to.

sources.title: Getting Started: Route Handlers
sources.claim: A route.ts route handler can receive the POST and forward it using Web Request/Response APIs.
